sections.html:
Take Clearfield County deeds to the Register and Recorder's Office on the courthouse's first level; the phone is 814-765-2641, extension 5012. Visitors can use six public workstations to look up what has been filed.

Its Recorder of Deeds division handles real estate paperwork along with notary bonds and commissions, UCC filings and military discharges, and it issues copies and certified copies.

For you as the seller, this is where the sale becomes official: recording a signed deed puts the new owner's title on the public record.

Before any deed is recorded, the county's Uniform Parcel Identifier office has to stamp it. The fee is $10 per parcel. Questions go to 814-765-2641, extension 2042. Deeds can be pre-approved for the UPI before the day of recording.

Sellers often assume recording is a single stop. It is two. Title agents typically send the deed over a day or two ahead, collect the stamp, and only then file with the recorder along with payment. Closing without a title company? Ask the county how pre-approval works before you pick a date.

The recorder's own deed checklist says the same thing: no UPI stamp from the Assessment Office, no recording.

Recording a deed or a mortgage runs $79.75. Names past four cost 50 cents each, and each page over four adds $2. For anything not listed, the Recorder of Deeds sets the fee.

What the Clearfield County recorder charges, by instrument
InstrumentRecording fee
Deed$79.75
Mortgage$79.75
Award of real estate or quiet title$69.75
Mortgage satisfaction piece, release, or assignment$59.75
Easement, right-of-way$59.75
Lease, agreement, power of attorney$18.50
Map$25, then $20 per added page
Copies, per page$0.50

The posted schedule is dated March 27, 2020, so call for the exact total before closing. Fees and transfer taxes are due at the moment of recording, by check to the Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: When a Statement of Value is needed
sections.html:
A Statement of Value comes into play when the deed omits the full price, when the home is given away, when you claim a tax exemption, or when a tax claim sale or sheriff's sale was involved. Inheritance by will does too. Sign and date it before filing.

The one exception is a transfer exempt only because the parties are close family: grandparent, parent, child, brother or sister.

The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent, paid at the recorder's window and often joined by a local tax. Buyer and seller share liability. Certain family transfers, inheritances by will or intestacy, and farms are exempt.

  • The deed carries the buyer's signed certificate of address.
  • It names the municipality and county where the property sits.
  • Land that crosses municipal or school district lines needs the percentage in each, so the local tax is split properly.
  • The acknowledgment date cannot be earlier than the date on the document.

Two search products are open to the public. Landex Remote is the full tool, with the same search criteria as the software in the courthouse, and it suits someone who searches often. Landex Webstore is the basic version for occasional use. It can search several counties at once and narrow results by county, instrument type and municipality. Viewing images requires a credit card payment. For help with the online products, call 717-274-5890.

Look up your own last recorded deed, plus any open mortgage, easement or right of way. Whatever turns up will also appear in the buyer's title search, so surprises are cheaper to handle now. A paid-off mortgage that was never released of record needs a satisfaction piece from the lender.

Documents come back unrecorded when the notary block is defective: no county or state, no date, no name of the signer or corporate officer, or no notary signature, seal or expiration date. The office will not take blanket assignments, releases or satisfactions.

  • A corrective or re-recorded document explains why and gets a fresh acknowledgment.
  • When one transaction has several documents, number them in recording order.
  • Foreign language documents need a written English translation.
  • Mailed packages need a stamped, addressed return envelope large enough to hold the document.

For electronic recording, the vendors are Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and CSC at 866-652-0111. A title company already set up with either one can skip the courier. Owners can also join the county's free Landex Record Alert, which sends an email or text if anyone tries to record a deed under your name or parcel number. You will need the parcel number shown under Map # on your tax invoice.

About 78,100 people lived here as of July 2025, a drop of 3.1 percent from the 2020 base. The county has 38,429 housing units, and 78.5 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. A typical owned home is worth $137,000, rent runs $791 a month, and household income is $62,152. DuBois is the biggest city; the county seat is Clearfield borough.

Gather these before anyone heads to the courthouse, and you will rarely get a package bounced.

  • The original deed, signed in ink and notarized with the notary's seal and expiration date showing.
  • Proof the UPI office has stamped it, at $10 for each parcel.
  • Buyer's address certificate and a clear municipality and county description.
  • A Statement of Value if the sale is a gift, an estate transfer or an exempt one.
  • One check for the recording fee and another for the realty transfer tax, payable to the Recorder of Deeds.

If anything is wrong, the office returns the package, and a corrective deed means paying to record again.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller at the recorder
sections.html:
Here is the usual order. You sign the deed in front of a notary at closing. The title agent or attorney arranges the UPI stamp, attaches the buyer's certificate of address, and writes checks for the recording fee and transfer tax. After that, the package reaches the recorder by courier, by mail with a return envelope, or electronically through a vendor.

Handling the sale on your own? Deliver the original signed deed with its UPI stamp, a Statement of Value if one applies, and checks made out to the Recorder of Deeds. Phone 814-765-2641, extension 5012 beforehand to learn the total for your page count.

Even a fast cash closing passes through the same two stops, the UPI office and then the recorder, so leave room for both.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a Clearfield County deed?
faqs.a: The base fee is $79.75 for a deed or mortgage. Extra names beyond four are 50 cents each and extra pages beyond four are $2 each. The posted schedule carries a March 27, 2020 date, so phone 814-765-2641, extension 5012 for the current total.

faqs.q: What is the UPI fee in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: The UPI stamp costs $10 per parcel and has to be on the deed first. Ask about pre-approval on 814-765-2641, extension 2042.

faqs.q: Is e-recording offered in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). Your title company will usually start the submission.

faqs.q: When is a Statement of Value required in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: File it if the deed leaves out the full price, if the house is a gift, if you claim an exemption, after a tax claim or sheriff sale, or when property passes by will. A transfer exempt only because of close family ties skips the form.

faqs.q: Who pays Pennsylvania realty transfer tax?
faqs.a: Buyer and seller are jointly liable for the 1 percent state tax. Your sales contract decides who actually pays what share. The recorder collects it when the deed goes in.
